title: SBE-BEAM technical limitations fail closed, rejecting any parameter value the module could not later undo
content:
A.3.5.2.4.4 defines a second, lower layer of protection: limitations that "apply independently of the bounding parameters set by Sky Governance," where "an attempt to use the SBE-BEAM in a manner that exceeds these limitations will revert."

The stated rationale for the five-year cap on `hop` is the clearest statement of the principle: it "prevents the Smart Burn Engine from being placed in a state in which its reward stream... can no longer be revived through the SBE-BEAM." Because `rewardsDuration` tracks `hop`, an absurdly long interval would stretch the staking reward stream out beyond any useful horizon — and since the module is the tool used to fix such a mistake, the mistake would be unfixable by the module that made it. The cap protects the *recoverability* of the mechanism, not the value of any parameter.

The other limits follow the same shape: `burn` above 100% "would cause the Smart Burn Engine to halt," and `kbump` must be a whole multiple of `RAY` or the transaction reverts, keeping the lot size in the protocol's standard fixed-point precision.

The design lesson is the layering. Governance-set bounds express current policy and can be voted looser; technical limitations express what would break or strand the machine and are not negotiable per-vote. Failing closed (revert) rather than clamping silently also means an operator error is visible as a failed transaction instead of an unintended state.
description: Enforced independently of governance bounds and by reverting rather than degrading: hop above five years would strand the reward stream, burn above 100% would halt the engine.
